main_text.p: felicitérque res gestas Cicero laudat. Partes illius tres sunt. Principium [illegible, ~7 letters] approbatione & laudatione constans facti Planci: Confirmatio laudationis rationes continés: à modo agendi: & effectis præclaris defumptas. Conclusio [illegible, ~6 letters] adhortatione facta, eademque, argumento sumpto à commodis, cùm publicis, tum priuatis, munita. Sententiæ esse tales poterunt.

I. O lætum nuncium, & cui merito [illegible, ~9 letters] debentur: de singulari tuo in communem patriam, Germaniam, amore ac studio: de celeritate incredi-bili conscribendi exercitum, præsisq; succurrendi: de virtute militum egregia: de victoria nobili atque præclara reportata.
II. Cæsi enim hostili in exercitu militum plurimi: duces ex prælio fugisse: desiderari ex nostris paucissimi dicuntur.
III. Itaque & summis in cœlum vsq; te exercitumq; tuū laudibus euehunt omnes, & faustis omi-nibus prosequuntur.

IIII. Sed interim eam in curam omni tibi incum-bendum esse studio cogitabis: vt quæ inchoata sunt feliciter, ad finem vsque perducantur, & depulsis iam primis, etiam extrema deleantur: atq; ita sacri-legijs templa: oppida direptionibus: vastationibus agri: cæde corpora: tecta incendijs: rapinis fortunæ liberentur.

page.notes: Two Greek words in the first paragraph and one Greek word in paragraph I are not legible on the scan and are marked as illegible. Printed "cui merito" is followed by a Greek word that I could not read letter by letter. The final line "liberentur," is the last line of the text block and is kept as running text. The right-hand printed page is not visible on this scan. Italic type runs from paragraph I to the end of the page, and the opening paragraph is roman.
